claims.text: The two container logs show a clear failure pattern in container_1445144423722_0020_01_000003, while the other container proceeds to completion.

In group [Group: container_1445144423722_0020_01_000003] the task attempt starts at 18:01:58 and is followed only by a cleanup event at 18:06:28, indicating that the container was terminated without any successful map or reduce output; this abrupt termination occurs after a five‑minute idle period with no further processing events.

In contrast, group [Group: container_1445144423722_0020_01_000005] records the full lifecycle of its task attempt—launch, execution on a node manager, and finally a cleanup event at 18:04:50 followed by an explicit “completed container” notification from the ResourceManager at 18:04:52—showing that the container finished normally.

The root‑cause hypothesis is that container_1445144423722_0020_01_000003 experienced an abnormal termination, likely due to a node‑manager failure or resource starvation on its assigned NM (MININT-FNANLI5), causing the container to be killed and cleaned up without completing its task.

This abnormal termination explains why only four log lines are present for that group, whereas the other group contains the full sequence of allocation, launch, execution, cleanup, and completion events.
